title: Match IPv6 addresses without compressed id from settings

timeline.body:
Make sure we normalize IPv6 addresses from the settings to the compressed form before we
match them with node ips. Node IPv6 addresses are all represented with the scope id
in the compressed form.

Closes #72091

timeline.message:
Match IPv6 addresses without compressed id from settings

Make sure we normalize IPv6 addresses from the settings to the compressed form before we
match them with node ips. Node IPv6 addresses are all represented with the scope id
in the compressed form.

Closes #72091
timeline.author: Artem Prigoda

timeline.body: Great, thanks Artem. My only comment is that I don't think we should normalise any filter that looks like it's an IP address, just the ones that use `matchByIP` when the filter executes. It's possible that folk will put things that might be an IP address in e.g. their node name, possibly with leading zeroes, but we shouldn't change how those things are matched.

timeline.message: Normalize ip addresses only when matching them by ip
timeline.author: Artem Prigoda

timeline.body: I suppose since it's important that we don't normalise things like node names we should have a test to assert that too.
Does this new mechanism also normalise IPv4 addresses by removing leading zeroes? That sounds desirable, it'd be good to have a test for this too to document this fact too.

reply.body: No, we don't support parsing IPv4 addresses with leading zeroes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/master/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/network/InetAddresses.java#L114
Ah excellent thanks for checking. Just IPv6 then.

timeline.body: I don't think this has anything to do with scope IDs? The scope ID is a suffix on the address of the form `%eth0`. How about `testNormalizesIPAddressFilters` (or `testNormalizesIPv6AddressFilters` and then a separate test for IPv4 addresses?
Prod changes look good to me, I left a few more thoughts about tests.
Sorry for the force-push noise, I was trying to disable force push commits for my Elasticsearch's fork.

timeline.body: Sorry I think I wasn't clear. What I meant was if, say, the node name is `fdbd:dc00:111:222::333` then this should not match the filter `xxx._name: fdbd:dc00:111:222:0:0:0:333` (and vice versa). In other words, a test that fails on 48132af26edcc317f8e71e6dc98f6a4277011fc2 to demonstrate why this isn't the right implementation.
